## Context / Problem

Epic 62dc's criteria 2, 3 and 4 are undelivered: `rebar create` does not surface semantically similar existing tickets, so agents re-file work that already has a ticket. ADR 0122 (`docs/adr/0122-similar-ticket-retrieval.md`, Accepted 2026-10-31) measured the retrieval candidates and is the binding evidence; this ticket is the container for building what it specifies.

The create-time advisory that exists today is a same-title journal only: `duplicate_create_warning` (`src/rebar/_commands/recent_creates.py:117`), gated by `verify.suggest_duplicate_tickets` (`:129`), matching on `title_norm` equality (`:103`). It catches byte-identical normalized titles and nothing else. ADR 0122 measured that stratum at 93.9% of recorded duplicate pairs and ruled a pooled score inadmissible; the 93 differing-title semantic pairs are what this work exists to catch.

**ADR 0122 decided retrieval quality, not portability.** It compared four candidates on this store and adopted `vector` — the Titan v2 embedding of a Haiku digest — reaching semantic recall@5 0.876 against the `fts5` baseline's 0.823 (p=0.0213, the only distinguishable win over the free baseline at k=5). What it did not consider is that rebar ships to environments with diverse model providers, or none. A retrieval path reachable only through one vendor's embedding endpoint would make the feature unavailable to most installations, which the blocking `project.portability` criterion forbids.

## Approach

Build retrieval in two tiers, with the portable one as the default and the measured one as an opt-in upgrade. The epic already requires the lexical fallback as a degradation path ("the suggestion field comes back empty or lexical-only with a diagnostic"); making it the default rather than only the failure mode is what makes the feature portable, and ADR 0122's own numbers show the cost of doing so is small and bounded.

- **Lexical tier — the default.** sqlite FTS5 with bm25 weights title 5.0 / description 1.0, the exact configuration ADR 0122 measured (`evals/similar-tickets/measure.py:389-391`). It needs no credentials, no network and no provider, so it works in every installation. It scores semantic recall@5 0.823 against `vector`'s 0.876, and it is *distinguishably better* than `vector` at lexical recall@10 (0.993 vs 0.972, p=0.0000), which ADR 0122 records as the reason `fts5` is not removed.
- **Embedding tier — opt-in.** The digest-and-embed path ADR 0122 adopted, reached through a configured embedding model rather than a hardcoded vendor call.

Portability is served by a seam rebar's runtime already ships, not a new one. pydantic-ai 1.107.9 — already the LLM runtime behind `src/rebar/llm/providers.py` — exposes a first-class embeddings API (`Embedder`, `EmbeddingModel`, `infer_embedding_model`, `KnownEmbeddingModelName`) with provider backends for `bedrock`, `openai`, `cohere`, `google`, `voyageai` and `sentence_transformers`, plus `OpenAIEmbeddingsCompatibleProvider` for arbitrary OpenAI-compatible endpoints. `sentence_transformers` runs locally with no credentials at all, and `TestEmbeddingModel` makes the tier testable offline without mocking a vendor. Dispatching on a `provider:model` string is the same shape rebar already uses for chat models, so the embedding tier is a config key over an existing mechanism rather than a new provider abstraction.

`bedrock:amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0` is the configured default because it is what ADR 0122 measured; an installation that cannot reach it configures another model or runs lexical-only, and in neither case does the feature become unavailable.

Surfacing reuses the advisory-field seam that `duplicate_warning` already proves end to end, rather than introducing a second create-time notification path. That seam carries an optional advisory on the same create result across all three surfaces — library and MCP as a result key (`src/rebar/types.py:276`, `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:179`), CLI on stderr so stdout stays pure (`src/rebar/_commands/composer.py:467`) — and is already described in `src/rebar/schemas/create_result.schema.json`. Reusing it means three-surface parity is met by extending a path that already has parity.

Sequencing follows the walking skeleton. The lexical tier delivers the whole user-visible feature — index, catch-up, three-surface surfacing, timing, branch purity — with no provider dependency, so the index and surfacing design is proven end to end before any paid call is wired in. The embedding tier then swaps the ranking function behind an interface that already has a working implementation and a measured baseline to beat.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rebar create` returns the top 5 similar existing tickets (id, alias, title, score) as an advisory field on all three surfaces — CLI `--output json`, the library `create_ticket` return dict, and MCP `create_ticket` — within a p95 of 500 ms on a synthetic store of at least 10,000 tickets when the index is warm. Checked by: the three-surface parity tests plus a timing test that asserts the generated store's size rather than assuming it.
- [ ] No derived search data is written to the `tickets` branch: after 100 creates and 100 reads against a test store, the branch contains only user event types. Checked by: an integration test asserting the event-type set of the branch after the run.
- [ ] A ticket created on a clone is findable by the next `create` on that same clone with no background process, daemon, MCP server or CI involved, via read-phase catch-up. Checked by: an integration test that runs the two creates in one process with no daemon, plus the measured cold-catch-up p95 recorded on this ticket (epic criterion 2's 500 ms bound is scoped to a warm index and does not cover this path).
- [ ] The feature is fully functional with no model provider configured and no network reachable: retrieval runs on the lexical tier and returns ranked results. Checked by: an integration test that unsets every provider credential env var and asserts a non-empty ranked result.
- [ ] Retrieval degrades to advisory-empty or lexical-only and never blocks a create: when the index is absent, catch-up fails, the configured embedding provider denies or errors, or the digest parse yields empty fields, the create still succeeds and the advisory field is empty or lexical-only with a diagnostic. Checked by: one test per failure mode asserting the create's exit status and the advisory contents.

## Child decomposition

- **Lexical tier, index and create-time surfacing** — the FTS5 index, the dir-hash freshness key, incremental catch-up, and the advisory field on all three surfaces. Delivers the portable default and every criterion above except the embedding tier's existence. This is the walking skeleton: it is the whole feature for an installation with no model provider.
- **Embedding tier over the pydantic-ai embeddings seam** — the digest step, the configured embedding model, the vector ranking, and the empties and retry counters ADR 0122 requires of any consumer. Delivers the opt-in upgrade from 0.823 to 0.876 semantic recall@5, and the provider-denial and digest-failure degradation paths.
- **Bedrock IAM widening for the Titan embedding model** — admits the configured default embedding model in this deployment. It gates the embedding tier's default configuration here; it does not gate the feature, which ships working on the lexical tier regardless.
